message.abstract:
<jats:p>
            Large language models (LLMs) have shown great success in code generation. LLMs take as the input a prompt and output the code. How to make prompts (i.e.,
            <jats:italic>Prompting Techniques</jats:italic>
            ) is a key question. Existing prompting techniques are designed for natural language generation and have low accuracy in code generation.
          </jats:p>
          <jats:p>
            In this article, we propose a new prompting technique named
            <jats:sc>AceCoder</jats:sc>
            . Our motivation is that code generation meets two unique challenges (i.e., requirement understanding and code implementation).
            <jats:sc>AceCoder</jats:sc>
            contains two novel mechanisms (i.e., guided code generation and example retrieval) to solve these challenges. ❶ Guided code generation asks LLMs first to analyze requirements and output an intermediate preliminary (e.g., test cases). The preliminary clarifies requirements and tells LLMs
            <jats:italic>“what to write.”</jats:italic>
            ❷ Example retrieval selects similar programs as examples in prompts, which provide lots of relevant content (e.g., algorithms, APIs) and teach LLMs
            <jats:italic>“how to write.”</jats:italic>
            We apply
            <jats:sc>AceCoder</jats:sc>
            to four LLMs (e.g., GPT-3.5, CodeGeeX) and evaluate it on three public benchmarks using the Pass@
            <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
              <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\(k\)</jats:tex-math>
            </jats:inline-formula>
            . Results show that
            <jats:sc>AceCoder</jats:sc>
            can significantly improve the performance of LLMs on code generation.
            <jats:italic>
              In terms of Pass@1,
              <jats:sc>AceCoder</jats:sc>
              outperforms the SOTA baseline by up to 56.4% in MBPP, 70.7% in MBJP, and 88.4% in MBJSP
            </jats:italic>
            .
            <jats:sc>AceCoder</jats:sc>
            is effective in LLMs with different sizes (i.e., 6B–13B) and different languages (i.e., Python, Java, and JavaScript). Human evaluation shows human developers prefer programs from
            <jats:sc>AceCoder</jats:sc>
            .
          </jats:p>
title:
<scp>AceCoder</scp>
            : An Effective Prompting Technique Specialized in Code Generation
